correctness.rationale: For d≥2 equality of partial maps forces every point in the domain to remain there after the first application; finiteness makes image and domain equal. For d=1 this follows directly from the equation. On a selected domain, nonadjacency including equality recovers its selected parts. Thus its automorphism group permutes blocks within each selected size and independently permutes their points. For an outer cycle of length ℓ, the necessary ℓ|d condition and the internal product equation h^(d/ℓ)=1 follow by iterating along the cycle; the products at other starts are conjugate. Choose all but one internal bijection and then solve for the last, giving exactly the frozen W recurrence. Likewise the T recurrence counts the cycle containing a designated point. The extension criterion is preservation of original part size on occupied parts. To verify sufficiency and the power equation simultaneously, label the unselected complement within each occupied original part by a common label set for its (selected size, original size) stratum. Extend by the unique matching of equal labels between complements, and fix unoccupied parts pointwise. This gives a group section for a fixed domain and preserves the order. Each domain profile now contributes its stated product, with one binomial choice factor per original part. Empty domain contributes 1; d=1 gives all partial identities. At rank two for d=2 only the transposition of vertices from unequal original part sizes fails to extend, giving the displayed sum and equivalence. The supplied checker was read; it constructs a set of restricted maps and compares its rank counts, rather than comparing that set elementwise with the formula. It was not executed.

For a stabilized domain and each fixed (selected size, capacity), choosing complement labels once makes each extension use the identity label map and unused blocks may be fixed. Hence the capacity-preserving domain group embeds by a section, which preserves all powers.

A marked outer cycle of length ℓ in H wr S_m has |H|^(ℓ−1) internal assignments per prescribed cycle product. Restricting to ℓ|d and to products of order dividing d/ℓ in H is the ordinary cycle-product enumeration; take H=S_s.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: There is no additional interaction between the power and extension obstructions in this family: after the same-domain restriction, the known pairs of block strata give both groups, and the section means no extra power filter in the extendible strata. Applying the generic cycle-product count and summing over domain choices gives both displayed polynomials. At rank two the only nonidentity is one transposition, inadmissible precisely across capacities. The implication uses actual structural passages and a direct deduction, not an inaccessible torsion-paper theorem.

originality.rationale: No exact duplicate power-marked polynomial was established. Nevertheless the fixed-domain specialization of the indexed equivalence-relation enumeration gives exactly the two relevant block-permutation groups. Restriction to d-torsion in each is a standard wreath-cycle count; the apparent extra extension constraint reduces mechanically to the same capacity condition by matching labels in equal-size complements. The rank-two formula is then just the count of unequal-capacity cross pairs, since the power equation removes rank-one domain-changing maps. This is a finding of direct implication/routine refinement, not a claim that the flagged exact formula appears verbatim or that the later indexed record has priority. The unavailable sources are not grounds for failure.

value.rationale: Prescribed powers and extension are well-motivated invariants, but here the prescribed-power constraint is just the usual wreath cycle filter on the already determined block groups and adds no obstruction to extension. The numerical defect is a direct cross-pair count once the capacities are known. The record does not establish a distinct nonroutine invariant or extension phenomenon beyond those consequences.
